text: {"lessons":["Selling A and C for gains, then buying A back at a higher price, shows that anchoring on my average cost can drive poor timing; I should base trades on current prospects and my target allocation.","A few months of modest account gains do not prove my choices are sound. I should evaluate results over a longer horizon and against a suitable benchmark, not react to single-month moves.","Because I check my account infrequently, I should use a simple, consistent review and rebalancing plan, while keeping enough cash and respecting risk limits rather than trading on regret or short-term price changes."]}
